issues.issue: The clause opens "Notwithstanding any said repossession" although no repossession right has been stated anywhere, and it waives damages on "the occurrence of an event of default under this section" though Section 5 never defines an event of default.

Section 5 contains no enumerated events of default and no repossession remedy, so this clause's cross-references to "said repossession" and "an event of default under this section" cannot be squared with the instrument read as a whole (cf. section 1.4, which also assumes forfeiture events "as herein set forth").
Fees are recoverable for enforcement "under this License Agreement or any related agreements", and "related agreements" is nowhere defined or identified.
The reference to "any related agreements" is in tension with section 7.7, which declares this License to be the entire agreement between the parties.

"Any other agreement signed contemporaneously between Licensor and Licensee" identifies no agreement and fixes no window for "contemporaneously", and "any default" is untethered to any defined event of default.
Importing defaults from other contemporaneous agreements cannot be reconciled with section 7.7's integration clause making this License "the entire agreement between the parties hereto".

"Shall be sent facsimile transmission-or overnight courier" omits the preposition and, more importantly, the clause gives a notice address only for the Licensor, leaving notice to the Licensee unprovided for.
The Licensor's address here (Apple Valley, MN 55337) contradicts the address given in the opening grant clause (7721 145th West, Apple Valley MN 55124).

The operative middle of the clause is unreadable garbled text, so the trigger and scope of the automatic revocation and reassignment of "any rights herein set forth" cannot be determined from the words used.

Revocation "if this Agreement is terminated" presupposes a right of termination that section 1.1 denies ("non-cancellable for any reason"), and no termination mechanism appears anywhere in the instrument.
"Renditions or enhancements of all System(s)" is undefined and, given the section 1.1 definition covering all ARP Wave intellectual property, the extent of what must be returned is uncertain.

Immediate return on termination "for any reason" is difficult to reconcile with section 1.3, which permits the Licensee to retain the System(s) after the original term, and with section 1.1's "non-cancellable" statement.

Survival after termination presupposes a termination right that section 1.1 forecloses by declaring the agreement "non-cancellable for any reason", though the clause is easily harmonised as contingent.
The clause requires strict compliance with "the ARP Unit Manual" and its "Cautionary and Warning language", neither of which is defined, attached or otherwise identified in the instrument.
It duplicates the protocol-compliance duty in section 3.1 but adds the Manual as a second, unincorporated standard, leaving which document controls unresolved.

Section 7.6 permits assignment of the Licensor's rights "without notice", while section 7.8 separately governs assignment of the Agreement; the two overlapping assignment clauses use different language but do not squarely conflict.

The integration clause declaring this License "the entire agreement" conflicts with section 5.2, which makes a default under "any other agreement signed contemporaneously" a default here, and with sections 5.2 and 7.9's references to "related agreements".

Section 7.8's bar on Licensee assignment restates section 1.4, and its grant of Licensor assignment rights duplicates section 7.6 (which dispenses even with notice); the overlap invites but does not compel an argument about which controls.

"All actions or proceedings relating to this Agreement or any related agreements" leaves both the reach of "relating to" (tort, trade-secret and non-party claims) and the undefined phrase "any related agreements" open, and the clause mixes consent to jurisdiction with a mandatory "must be litigated" venue command.

The forum clause binds "each party", but the instrument never names the Licensee other than as "you" in the opening grant, so whether it binds the individual signatory or his company must be resolved from elsewhere in the document.
The judicial-reformation sentence directs that an overbroad provision "shall be sufficiently narrowed so as to make it enforceable" without any standard for how far to narrow it.
